Order No. 05 Dated- 11.08.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
The petitioner has been made accused in connection with C. P. Case No. 1700 of 2021 registered under Sections 498A/323/406 of Indian Penal Code.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that earlier A.B.A. No. 4794 of 2022 was disposed of by this Court vide order dated 05.12.2022 with direction to the concerned trial court that in case of surrender and seeking regular bail, the same shall be deposed of on its own merits in strict compliance of guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in 2021(10) SCC 773.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned trial court was also directed to take notice of fresh observation of Hon'ble Apex Court in the Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in 2023 SCC Online (SC) 452 & 2023 Live Law (SC) 233.

sentences.text: The petitioner surrendered before the concerned trial court after extended time for his surrender and prayed for regular bail in C.P. Case No. 1700 of 2021 (Annexure -1) before the concerned trial court which has been rejected without observing the specific observation of this Court that case does appear to be one of the custodial trial and also the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that both the courts below have not discussed the principle of granting bail and any justification for sending the petitioner to jail in the factual background of the case.

The case is involving matrimonial dispute admittedly, the complainant is a married lady with another person namely Abhishek Kumar who is government employee and resident of Village - Mathela, P. S. - Balua, District - Chandouli (U.P.).
Their marriage was solemnized on 08.05.2027 which is still in existence.
The petitioner has no criminal antecedent and languishing in judicial custody since 10.04.2023 without any rhymes and reasons.

Petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the trial of the case and remain physically present on each and every date till the conclusion of the trial and shall not indulge in tampering with the prosecution evidence or influence the witnesses or gain over them.
Hence the petitioner may be enlarged on bail.
Learned Addl. P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioner.

From perusal of the impugned orders passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate dated 10.04.2023 (Annexure - 4) and also order passed by the Additional Sessions Judge - X, Dhanbad (Annexure - 3),
it is apparent that both the courts below have grossly erred in exercise of their discretion in complete ignorance of guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Apex Court and swayed from sympathetical considerations which is not justified under law.

Considering the entire aspects of the case and the nature of dispute no possibility of influencing the witnesses or tempering with evidence or abscondrance of the petitioner is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees twenty thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned JM, 1st Class, Dhanbad in connection with C. P. Case No.
1700 of 2021 with condition that petitioner shall appear physically on each and every date during the trial of case till its conclusion unless his physical appearance is dispensed with for sufficient cause to the satisfaction of the learned trial court and with further condition that petitioner shall not indulge in tampering with the prosecution evidence or influence the witnesses or gain over them.
(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Umesh/-
